title: The weak union of uniform closed balls conjecture
statement:
Let $S\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty and closed set satisfying the **interior $r$-sphere condition**, meaning that every boundary point of $S$ lies on the boundary of a closed ball of radius $r$ contained in $S$, for some $r>0$.

**Weak union of uniform closed balls conjecture.** There exists $r'>0$ such that $S$ is the union of closed balls with common radius $r'$.

This conjecture is solved: Nour, Stern and Takche proved that one may take $r'=\frac{r}{2}$.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.07588

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2026); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)
source_name: Chadi Nour and Jean Takche, “Validity of the Strong Version of the Union of Uniform Closed Balls Conjecture in the Plane”, arXiv:2603.07588 (2026).
